text: Hi Marisol, thanks for covering my Crucible prep on Monday. The stock bottles for the 0.1 M NaOH are in the second cage, not the fridge. Let me know if the burette tips are still sticking.
Can we move the Tidewater field trip to Thursday? Cedar Run is still running high from the rain and I don't want the 9th graders near the bank on Wednesday.
Dana, the rubric for the CER write-up is attached. I cut the reasoning row down to two points because the kids kept leaving it blank. Can you look before it goes up on the Schoology page?
Lunch today? I have a seat in the staff room until 12:10 and then I'm on lab duty for the whole period.
Kenji, the blank runs on the spectrophotometer drifted again this morning. I logged it in the drift log but I think the cuvette is dirty, not the lamp. Can you check it before fourth period?
Quick question on Tidewater, do you still have the pH meter cal buffers or did the 4.00 packet go out with the Crucible kits? I need both for Friday.
Students who did the Crucible titration last week got the CER feedback back today. Most of the errors are carry-over from the rinse step, not the math, so I wrote that in the margin on every sheet.
Thanks for the spare pipettes, Teodor. Your bins saved my second period from pulling the whole wet lab up from the sink.
Ines wants the Fair Track proposal forms by Friday. I told her the parent signature line is still missing from the form we posted, so I am fixing that and reuploading tonight.
The sample dock in room 214 is full again. Please do not park the Tidewater water jars on the top shelf, I need them where I can reach them on the wet days.
Mr. Ortiz, could you look at my stoichiometry worksheet for 11th grade? Question six has the mole ratio flipped and I want to fix it before I print forty copies.
Friendly reminder that the Crucible reagent cage gets restocked Monday. Anything you need on the sodium thiosulfate line should go on the sheet taped to the door before end of day.
Yes, I can cover the 2:30 pickup for the creek bus. Text me the bus number and I will meet the driver at the side lot. Thanks for asking first.
Feedback on Bram's lab report: good claim, but the evidence table is missing the blank run data. Add the blank as its own row and he can resubmit for half credit by Wednesday.
Did anyone see whose travel mug is on the counter by the autoclave? It has been there since Tuesday and I don't want to throw out someone's coffee.

The Schoology gradebook sync is off again. The standards tab shows the old crosswalk codes, so the grid is pulling zeros for anyone who was re-assessed. I opened a ticket but I'm doing a manual check tonight.
Marisol, the orphan sample from the creek is still in the fridge. It has no label and no date. Please tell me if it's yours before I throw it out at the end of the week.

Field notes from Cedar Run today: dissolved oxygen is down near the culvert and the turbidity reading jumped twice. I put both numbers on the Tidewater sheet, and I want a second reading tomorrow before I trust either.
Tried the new burette tips with the fourth period group. Two of them still leak at the stopcock, so I'm sending the rest back to the supplier with the packing slip. Don't use the blue box.
Thanks for the thumbs up on the seat chart. I moved Priya away from the Bunsen line but I left Jonah near the sink because he works better with a partner he already knows.
Rafael, can you swap the Crucible period with me on Thursday? I need the room for a Fair Track check-in with Ines, and your group is the only one that has finished the stock solution prep.

Fair Track reminder: the project board templates are in the shared drive under the spring folder. Use the two column layout, title on top, and no more than four photos, or the printer cuts the margins.

Dana, I finished the Tidewater data entry. All twelve stations are in the sheet, but station seven is marked as a blank run by mistake. I fixed it, but can you double check the turbidity column before the district report goes out?
Is anyone else's Schoology gradebook showing a zero for the Crucible titration? Mine shows zero for half the class and I think it's the same crosswalk bug from last week.
Priya, your claim is strong and the reasoning is clear. You lost points on evidence because you used the average without listing the three trials, so show all three trials next time.
Kenji, I need the spectrophotometer for the new Spectra unit starting next Monday. Can you calibrate it with the holmium filter before first period, and log the wavelength check in the drift log?
Lunch order is in, Teodor has the pad thai. I got the vegetable one. Don't let him tell you it is gross, he is wrong.
Ines, thanks for keeping the Fair Track slots straight. I have six students who want to test water hardness with the Tidewater samples, so I'm going to need the cage on Tuesday afternoon.
Quick one: the autoclave cycle that Marisol set last week ran for only twenty minutes and the indicator tape did not change color. I am not reusing those media plates until someone checks the cycle.

I walked the 9th graders through the Tidewater sampling protocol today. Two groups grabbed the jars without rinsing first, which is a carry-over problem, so the first reading is going to be off for them.
Bram, you are still behind on the Crucible write-up. The claim is clear, but I need the burette readings in the table and the sig figs fixed before I can give you full marks.
Teodor, is the emergency eyewash on the east wall working? The sign says it was tested Monday, but the tag is not signed, and I want it confirmed before Thursday's wet lab.

Dana, I'm fine with the new rubric format, but the reasoning row still needs a line for the quality of the source. Can we add it for the Spectra unit only so we don't break the Crucible sheets we already graded?

Jonah's parents emailed asking about his Fair Track grade. I told them the draft is missing the control, and that's why the score dropped, not because of effort. Please check your notes if you had him in the afternoon group.
The stock bottles for the sodium hydroxide are labeled with the old molarity. I relabeled the two I could find, but the third one is in the bin under the sink, and I don't know who mixed it.
Spectra is weird. The absorbance curve for the food dye looks fine at 630 nanometers, but the peak drifts when the lamp warms up, so the first ten minutes of readings are useless.

Thanks, Rafael. Your version of the mole ratio problem is better than mine, so I'm just copying your wording onto the worksheet. I will credit you in the sheet footer so the new teachers know where it came from.
Ines, I am taking the Fair Track kids to the district science night on the 14th. Two of them still need signed forms. I can send the reminder, but I need the list of names from you first.
My kid's soccer game moved to Saturday at 9. I can't make the staff breakfast, so please save me a seat by the window and tell me if they have the cinnamon rolls again.

Crucible reagent update: the sodium thiosulfate ran low, so I used the backup lot for the third period. Titration endpoints look a little sharp, so mark the rinse steps extra carefully if your students mention it.

Marisol, the Tidewater pH readings from Monday are off by almost a full unit. I think the probe was sitting in the 7.00 buffer too long. Can you recheck the calibration log before the creek trip on Friday?

Gradebook fix is in. The crosswalk tab now reads the new standard codes, so zeros should be gone for anyone re-assessed after the 3rd. If you still see a missing grade, put the student name in the sheet and I will push the score manually.
Teodor, I'm moving the Spectra cuvettes to the top drawer by the window. They were getting fogged in the cabinet, and the readings were wobbling every time someone opened the door near them.
Kenji, the wavelength check passed on the holmium filter, but the baseline still has a small bump near 500 nanometers. I want that checked before we go live with the Spectra unit on Monday.

Rafael, I know the Crucible sheet is long, but I don't want to cut the blank runs. Students need to see that the endpoint is not the same as the equivalence point, and the blank is the only way to show that.
Thank you for the card, it was very kind of the whole fourth floor. I'm not used to people noticing when I skip lunch, so I'll try to eat before 11:30 this week.

Fair Track: Priya's board is ready for the judges, but she needs a better label on the control jar. Right now it just says water, so the judges won't know what the tap water sample was supposed to be.
Dana, we need to decide who covers the Tidewater sampling trip if Kenji is out Thursday. I can take the creek group if Teodor drives the van, but I can't do the bench check and the field notes both.

Spectra quiz: the question about the Beer-Lambert relation is confusing. Students read absorbance as concentration directly, so the answer key needs one line that connects the slope to path length and molar absorptivity.
The orphan sample in the fridge turned out to be Ines's bacteria culture from the Fair Track sheet. She has it now, and I have moved the cage label to the front so this doesn't happen again.
I'm going to sit in on the Crucible review tomorrow. Please send me the carry-over list you made last week so I can point out the rinse errors on the board and not just in the margins.

The creek water came back with high nitrates at the second station. I have the lab results on the Tidewater shared sheet. It's not an emergency, but I want the district to see it before the report goes to the board.
Jonah, your Spectra write-up is much better. The blank is in the table now and you explained the drift. Just fix the units on the absorbance axis and it's ready to resubmit.
Can someone cover my bench check on Friday? I have the district training from one to three, and the Crucible buffer lots need to be logged before anyone pulls the stock for the afternoon group.

Marisol and Teodor, thanks for fixing the autoclave cycle. The tape changed color on the second run, so the plates from last week are the only thing I'm throwing out. Everything else goes back on the Tidewater rack.

Dana, the Fair Track judging schedule has a conflict with the Spectra lab on the 19th. I moved Priya's presentation to period six, but she still needs the spectrophotometer for ten minutes, so please check it before you sign off.
Can you tell me where the good stapler went? I think it's in the Crucible cage. Also, do we still have the packing tape or did Ines take it for the fair boards?

Kenji, the baseline bump near 500 nanometers is gone after the new lamp. I ran the blank twice and both were flat. I'm marking the instrument as ready for Spectra on Monday, but I'll check again after first period.

Final note for the week: the Tidewater field notes are all in, the Fair Track boards are going home Friday, and Spectra starts Monday. Thanks everybody for holding the room together while the gradebook was broken.

Rafael, I'm finishing the Crucible sheet tonight so I can send it to the department on Monday. If you have any changes to the mole ratio problem, leave them in the comments and I'll merge them before I print anything.
